question: Do each group's most group-specific rules stay specific in later periods, and are a few extra group-specific slots worth more than the next global rules?
practical_meaning: On top of one store-wide display, is it worth reserving a few slots per customer group for the combinations that group especially buys?

candidate_rules_per_group.in_group: joint >= 20 orders from >= 10 distinct customers, largest single-customer share of joint orders <= 0.5, antecedent >= 20 orders, confidence >= 0.40, lift >= 1.3, 3-category increment >= 10 percentage points; no relative support threshold
candidate_rules_per_group.outside: outside = the other groups of the same system; outside antecedent >= 20 orders from >= 10 customers
candidate_rules_per_group.advantage_pp: 100 * [(conf_in - base_in(consequent)) - (conf_out - base_out(consequent))], base = consequent count / orders in that scope
candidate_rules_per_group.ranking: advantage desc, joint desc, confidence desc, rule_id asc
candidate_rules_per_group.de_duplication: unit = combination; keep the first directed rule of a combination; skip a combination that is a superset of a kept one
candidate_rules_per_group.random_controls: every seed of A1 (primary), S and A2 builds its own lists with exactly the same procedure

E5a_specificity_retention.evaluated_rules: the up to 30 directed rules (10 per group) of each system
E5a_specificity_retention.direction_retained: future advantage > 0; a rule whose advantage is undefined in the future (no antecedent in or out of the group) counts as not retained; the denominator is all selected rules
E5a_specificity_retention.effect_retention_ratio: median of future advantage / Discovery advantage
E5a_specificity_retention.evidence_retained: future advantage >= 5pp; target antecedent >= 20 orders from 10 customers, target joint >= 10 orders from 5 customers, largest customer share of target joint <= 0.5; outside antecedent >= 20 orders from 10 customers; one-sided customer-cluster t test of advantage > 0 with BY q <= 0.05 inside the system's own rules
E5a_specificity_retention.variance: advantage = d_in - d_out with d = J/A - C/N; customer influence u_i = (J_i - conf*A_i)/A - (C_i - base*N_i)/N per side, var = m/(m-1) * sum u_i^2, sides added (disjoint customers), df = min(m_in, m_out) - 1
E5a_specificity_retention.primary_statistic: direction-retention rate pooled over the system's rules
E5a_specificity_retention.comparison: real vs A1 seeds, empirical p

validation_confirmation.rule: a Discovery-selected rule is confirmed if its Validation advantage > 0 and the target and outside evidence counts of E5a are met (no significance requirement)
validation_confirmation.applies_to: real groups and every random seed identically

E5b_marginal_gain.base_list: G's top B0 combinations under P5 with E10 V3 de-duplication
E5b_marginal_gain.hybrid: a customer of group g sees G's top B0 plus their group's specific combinations that are not already in, or supersets of, G's top B0 (k_g' of them)
E5b_marginal_gain.comparator: the same customer sees G's top B0 + k_g' combinations
E5b_marginal_gain.gain: coverage(hybrid) - coverage(comparator) over all evaluated orders; paired customer bootstrap interval

lists.confirmed: only Validation-confirmed rules; evaluated on Validation only descriptively, because confirmation used Validation; its real test is the Test run

E5b_marginal_gain.comparison: real vs A1 seeds, empirical p

periods.discovery: build candidate lists; describe them; no conclusions
periods.validation: E5a Discovery->Validation (first test of specificity); confirmation; E5b preliminary with both lists
periods.test: later single run: H_E5a (Discovery->Test retention) and H_E5b (confirmed-list gain), plus Validation->Test retention of confirmed rules

interpretation_rules.group_preference_real: E5a direction retention above the A1 95th percentile (empirical p <= 0.05)
interpretation_rules.slots_worth_it: E5b gain > 0, paired interval excludes 0, and gain above the A1 95th percentile
interpretation_rules.report_per_group: results are also reported per group; if only C0 passes, the claim is limited to C0
